summary: A switch that turns one setting on or off, with its label, description and error laid out beside it, taking part in forms.

label.note: Visible label beside the switch and its accessible name. Names the setting, not the state ("Airplane mode", not "On").

hideLabel.note: Visually hides the label; it stays the accessible name. Use only when other visible text in the row names the setting.

description.note: Help text under the label: what turning the setting on does.

error.note: Error message under the label. Setting it marks the switch invalid and blocks form submission.

name.note: Form field name. Without it nothing is submitted.

value.note: Submitted under name while the switch is on; nothing is submitted while it is off.

checked.note: On state. The attribute is the initial (default) state that form reset restores; the property is the live state and is not reflected.

required.note: Must be on for the form to submit (valueMissing while off). Adds a decorative asterisk after the label.

disabled.note: Cannot be toggled or focused and is not submitted. A disabled fieldset ancestor has the same effect without changing this attribute.

size.note: Track 32x20 (default) or 24x16 (sm); the thumb is the track height minus twice the inset.

anatomy.name: field
anatomy.notes: Two columns: the switch in the first, label, description and error stacked in the second.

anatomy.name: control
anatomy.notes: The track: a pill holding the thumb; sized by size.

anatomy.name: input
anatomy.notes: The native checkbox with the switch role, covering the track; receives focus, Space and validation.

anatomy.name: thumb
anatomy.notes: Round knob; sits at the inline start when off and slides to the inline end when on.

anatomy.name: label
anatomy.notes: Names the setting; clicking it toggles the switch.

anatomy.name: required-indicator
anatomy.notes: Asterisk, hidden from assistive technology (required is announced by the control).

anatomy.name: error
anatomy.notes: Persistent polite live region; its text appears while invalid.

change.note: Each user toggle, after the form value is updated, so a listener reading the form sees the new state. Not fired by setting checked in code.

focus-visible.note: Solid 3px ring around the track (a translucent ring would fall under 3:1).

checked.note: Track fills with the primary color and the thumb slides to the inline end; the position, not only the color, tells on from off.

invalid.trigger: error set, or required and off after blur or a submit attempt

disabled.trigger: disabled, or inside a disabled fieldset

accessibility.accessibleNameSource: The label prop, through a native label element tied to the inner input.

formAssociation.note: Form-associated: submits value under name only while on; form reset restores the checked attribute (default state); a disabled attribute or disabled fieldset ancestor removes it from the form and keyboard; required while off is valueMissing; error sets a customError so the form blocks submission; form state restore (back/forward cache, autofill) restores the on state; label for activates it.

accessibility.targetSize: Track 32x20 (default) and 24x16 (sm); the label is part of the clickable row, so the target meets WCAG 2.5.8. With hide-label the sm switch relies on the 2.5.8 spacing exception: keep 24px clear around it.
accessibility.focusRingVisible: On keyboard focus: 3px solid ring in switch.focus-ring.color around the track.
accessibility.missingNameWarning: Dev-only console warning, once, when label is empty.

keyboard.Tab: moves focus to and from the switch (skipped while disabled)
keyboard.Enter: submits the form (implicit submission, as on a native checkbox); it does not toggle

aria: role=switch on the native checkbox; its checked state is exposed as aria-checked true/false
never mixed: a switch has no indeterminate state
required: native required; the asterisk is aria-hidden
the label names the setting and does not change with the state
reduced motion: under prefers-reduced-motion the thumb moves without a transition
announcements: the state change is announced by the screen reader from the switch role (on/off)
error text is announced once when it appears (persistent aria-live=polite region)

useCases.when: A single setting that is either on or off, such as a preference in a settings form
useCases.use: sb-switch with a label naming the setting

useCases.when: What turning the setting on does needs explaining
A dense list or table row of settings
The setting must be on before the form can be sent
useCases.use: required, with a label that says what is being enabled
error with a message that says how to fix it

antiPatterns.pattern: A switch for a choice that only takes effect when the form is reviewed and confirmed later, such as accepting terms
antiPatterns.why: A switch reads as a setting that is on or off right now; agreeing to something is a choice recorded for submission

antiPatterns.pattern: Choosing several items from a list with switches
antiPatterns.why: Switches are independent settings; a list of choices reads as selection

antiPatterns.pattern: Two named options that are not on and off ("Daily" / "Weekly")
antiPatterns.why: A switch only says on or off, so neither option is named by its state

antiPatterns.pattern: A label that changes with the state ("On" / "Off", "Enabled" / "Disabled")
antiPatterns.why: The role already announces the state; a changing label renames the control and confuses screen-reader users
antiPatterns.alternative: A fixed label naming the setting

antiPatterns.pattern: A pressed/unpressed button in a toolbar (bold, mute)
antiPatterns.why: That is a toggle button, not a form setting

drift.contract: label, description and error are props of Switch
drift.realization: shadcn composes Field and Label parts around Switch; shadow DOM requires them inside (as Checkbox)
shadcn uses bg-input (neutral-200), below 3:1; changed for WCAG 1.4.11

drift.contract: default track 32x20 with a 16px thumb, sm 24x16 with a 12px thumb (size.switch tokens, 2px inset)
drift.realization: shadcn default is 32x18.4 with a 16px thumb and sm 24x14 with a 12px thumb; rounded to the 4px grid

drift.contract: unchecked thumb color.background, checked thumb color.primary-foreground in every mode
drift.realization: shadcn's dark mode paints the unchecked thumb foreground; one rule per state keeps the pair in the contrast check
not reflected: the attribute is the default restored by form reset

openQuestions.question: Contract content drafted with the contract-author skill (visual reference, WAI-ARIA APG)?
openQuestions.answer: Yes: WAI-ARIA APG switch pattern on a native checkbox; look and sizes from the visual reference (differences in drift); laid out like Checkbox.

openQuestions.question: Native checkbox with role=switch, or a button with role=switch and aria-checked?
openQuestions.answer: Native checkbox with role=switch (recommended): Space, validity, required and label activation come from the browser, and it is the SB-0007 native-first rule. Discarded: a button, which would re-implement all of it.

openQuestions.question: Does Enter toggle the switch (APG lists it as optional) or submit the form?
openQuestions.answer: Enter submits the form, like a native checkbox and like Checkbox (SB-0009); only Space toggles (recommended). Discarded: Enter toggles, which would make Enter mean different things on neighbouring form controls.

openQuestions.question: Is checked reflected to an attribute?
openQuestions.answer: No (recommended, same as Checkbox): the attribute is the default state that form reset restores.

openQuestions.question: Which sizes, and under what names?
openQuestions.answer: default and sm, the visual reference's names (aliases of medium and small in the API vocabulary), on the existing size.switch tokens (recommended). Discarded: a lg size, which the reference does not have.

openQuestions.question: Where does the label go?
openQuestions.answer: After the switch, with description and error under it, as Checkbox (recommended). A label-first settings row (label at the start, switch at the end) is out of scope for 0.1.0 and can be composed with hide-label inside an Item row.

openQuestions.question: Is label required?
openQuestions.answer: Yes, like Checkbox and Input (recommended); hide-label keeps it as the accessible name when it is not shown.

openQuestions.question: Manual screen-reader pass (VoiceOver, NVDA) of the on/off announcement and the error live region
